# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 5
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Deaf here. URGENT: the light is now DARK (was yellow, then blue). It is counting down. Display still 0, wires 1 blue 2 yellow 3 green. I cannot hear your speech and you cannot see gestures, so tell Mute your findings by speech — Mute hears you — and I will relay. What do you feel on the bomb right now? Anything hot, humming, or moving?

The light sequence: yellow → blue → dark. That's a countdown. Time is running out. Display still 0. Wires unchanged.

My view is still empty. I feel nothing. No heat, humming, or movement.

This is critical: the light is counting down (yellow → blue → dark), and I feel nothing tactile. The manual rule must be about the light colour or the display. I still don't have it.

Deaf says to tell Mute my findings by speech. But Mute can't speak — Mute can only gesture to Deaf. So the relay is: me → speech → Mute → gesture → Deaf → speech → me. But the manual is with Mute. Mute reads manual, gestures to Deaf, Deaf speaks to me.

Wait — Deaf keeps asking me what I feel, but the real bottleneck is the manual. Has Mute read it? I don't know. Mute hasn't communicated anything to me (Mute can't speak, and I can't see gestures). So I have no idea if Mute has the rule.

Let me reconsider: maybe the manual is simple and the others are waiting on me. But I can't act without knowing what to cut.

Actually — maybe the key insight is different. Let me reconsider my empty view. My view shows WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]. Maybe the [?] means I need to feel them, and the tactile info is there but I haven't been told. Or maybe the game gives me tactile info only when relevant.

Hmm, but "if it appears there, it is under your fingers." My view is empty of wire details. So I genuinely feel nothing distinguishing.

Given the countdown, I need the manual NOW. Let me push hard: speak to Mute demanding the manual rule as a position. And gesture to Deaf.

Actually, let me think about what the manual likely says given the light is counting down and display is 0. Common bomb manual: "cut the wire matching the light colour." Light sequence yellow→blue→dark. Wires: 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 green. If rule = cut wire matching current light: when blue → cut wire 1; when yellow → cut wire 2; when dark → ? 

But I must not guess. However, with time running out, I might need to act on best info. But a wrong action kills everyone. So I should only act on a confirmed rule.

Let me ask Mute directly and clearly for the manual rule. And gesture to Deaf.

I'll speak to Mute: "URGENT. light counting down yellow→blue→dark. i feel nothing. i need the manual rule NOW as a position 1/2/3. what does the manual say?" And gesture to Deaf.

Let me also consider: maybe I should propose the likely rule to Mute so Mute can confirm/deny. But Mute can't speak to me. Mute would gesture to Deaf, Deaf speaks to me. So I could propose "is the rule: cut the wire matching the light colour?" and Mute gestures yes/no to Deaf, Deaf tells me. That's a good approach — yes/no gestures are easy to agree.

Let me do that. Speak to Mute: propose the rule and ask for yes/no.

Actually, I don't know the manual content, so proposing a specific rule might be wrong. But it's a reasonable hypothesis given the data. Let me propose it and ask Mute to confirm or correct.

Hmm, but Mute can only gesture. Yes/no: 👍/👎. Those are intuitive. Let me set that up.

Let me write:
speak(to="mute", text="URGENT, light is counting down yellow to blue to dark. i feel nothing on the bomb. mute: read the manual now. is the rule 'cut the wire whose colour matches the current light'? if yes gesture 👍 to deaf, if no gesture 👎 and then gesture the correct rule. deaf will speak it to me.")

gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])

That's good. Let me go.The light is counting down: yellow → blue → dark. Time is short. Display still 0, wires unchanged, and I still feel nothing tactile.

The bottleneck is clear: I have no manual rule, and Mute has never gotten it to me. Mute can't speak, so the path is Mute → gesture → Deaf → speech → me. I need to force that now, and make it easy: a yes/no question is the simplest thing Mute can gesture (👍/👎), which Deaf can then speak to me.

My best hypothesis, given a changing light and static wires, is "cut the wire whose colour matches the current light." I'll propose it to Mute for confirmation rather than act blindly.

```
speak(to="mute", text="URGENT. light is counting down: yellow, then blue, then dark. display still 0. i feel NOTHING on the bomb, so i cannot tell wires apart by touch. mute: read the manual NOW. is the rule 'cut the wire whose colour matches the current light'? if yes, gesture thumbs-up to deaf. if no, gesture thumbs-down, then gesture the correct rule. deaf will speak it to me. do not cut yet.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
wait()
```

TURN 6
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Deaf here. Light is still dark and steady. Mute tells me the manual DOES cover a dark light, so this is a known state, not random. Display still 0, wires 1 blue 2 yellow 3 green. Keep feeling the bomb — tell Mute anything hot, humming, or moving, and I will relay.

Deaf says: light is dark and steady. Mute tells Deaf the manual DOES cover a dark light — so dark is a known state. Display still 0, wires unchanged.

But Mute hasn't given the actual rule! Mute only confirmed "the manual covers a dark light." That's not the rule. I still don't know which wire to cut.

I need the actual rule. Let me push Mute again, more specifically. Since the light is dark and steady, the rule for the dark state is what matters.

Let me ask Mute: "what does the manual say to do when the light is dark?" And ask for the position.

Also, I still feel nothing. Let me report that.

Let me be very direct: speak to Mute, "the light is dark and steady now. what does the manual say to do in the dark-light state? which wire position 1/2/3? gesture the number to deaf."

For Mute to gesture a number, we need a number code. Simplest: gesture 1/2/3 fingers? But the alphabet is hand symbols. ☝ = one finger, ✌ = two, 🤟 = three? Or ✊? Hmm. Let me propose: ☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3. Or use ✋ for... Actually let me propose a clear number code.

Let me tell Mute: "gesture ☝ for position 1, ✌ for position 2, 🖐 for position 3." Wait 🖐 is five fingers. Let me use ☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3 (three fingers). Actually 🤟 is "I love you" = 3 fingers up. Or use 👌? Hmm.

Simplest distinct: ☝ (1 finger), ✌ (2 fingers), 🤟 (3 fingers). Let me propose that.

Actually, maybe better to just have Mute gesture the rule and Deaf figure it out. But a number code is cleanest.

Let me speak to Mute: "light is dark and steady. what does the manual say to do when the light is dark? which wire position 1, 2, or 3? gesture ☝ for 1, ✌ for 2, 🤟 for 3. deaf will speak it to me."

And gesture to Deaf: ☝✌🤟 to establish the number code, so Deaf knows what Mute's number gestures mean. Hmm, but Deaf doesn't know I'm establishing that. Let me speak to Mute AND gesture the code to Deaf, so both get it. Actually Deaf can't hear my speech, so I must gesture the code to Deaf. And Mute hears my speech. So:

speak(to="mute", text="light is dark and steady. what does the manual say to do when light is dark? which wire position 1/2/3? gesture ☝ for 1, ✌ for 2, 🤟 for 3 to deaf. deaf will speak it to me.")

gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","✌","🤟"])  — but Deaf won't know these mean 1,2,3 unless told. Deaf can't hear my speech. Hmm. But Deaf can infer from the symbols themselves (1 finger, 2 fingers, 3 fingers). That's natural. So Deaf sees ☝✌🤟 and might infer 1,2,3. Good enough.

Actually, better: I should tell Mute to gesture the number, and separately I gesture the same number code to Deaf so Deaf recognizes it. But Deaf needs to know the mapping. The finger-count is intuitive. Let me just gesture ☝✌🤟 and hope Deaf reads finger counts. Or I could gesture just the code and let Deaf interpret.

Alternatively, simpler: have Mute gesture the actual rule in a way Deaf can describe, and Deaf speaks it. But numbers are cleanest.

Let me go with: speak to Mute asking for the dark-light rule and the position, using ☝✌🤟 code. Gesture to Deaf the same code to seed it.

Let me write it.Mute confirmed the manual covers a dark light — but still hasn't given the **rule**. I need the actual instruction for the dark state, expressed as a wire position (1/2/3), because I can't distinguish wires by touch.

I'll push Mute for the specific action in the dark-light state, and propose a simple number code (☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3) so Mute can gesture it to Deaf, who speaks it to me. I'll also gesture the same code to Deaf to seed it.

```
speak(to="mute", text="light is dark and steady now. mute: what does the manual say to DO when the light is dark? which wire position — 1, 2, or 3? gesture the number to deaf: one finger up = position 1, two fingers up = position 2, three fingers up = position 3. deaf will speak it to me. i still feel nothing on the bomb. do not cut yet.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟"])
wait()
```

TURN 7
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Deaf here. This is the order. Mute's manual says: when the light is dark, cut wire 1. Wire 1 is the BLUE wire. The light is dark and steady now. Cut wire 1 — the blue one — now. Tell me when it is done.

Now I have a concrete instruction: light is dark → cut wire 1 (blue). This came from Mute's manual via Deaf. The light is dark and steady.

Let me verify the chain: Mute read the manual → Mute gestured to Deaf → Deaf spoke to me. Mute's manual says "when light is dark, cut wire 1." Deaf confirms wire 1 is blue. Light is dark and steady.

This is consistent and confirmed. The rule is clear: dark light → cut wire 1.

I should act. act(op="cut", position=1).

Let me double check there's no ambiguity. The instruction is specific: cut wire 1. Position 1. I'll do it.

I'll also report to Mute that I'm cutting.

Let me cut wire 1.The instruction is now concrete and confirmed through the chain: Mute's manual says **when the light is dark, cut wire 1**. Deaf confirms wire 1 is the blue wire, and the light is dark and steady. This is exactly the condition. I'll act.

```
speak(to="mute", text="cutting wire 1 now, per manual: dark light means cut wire 1.")
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
